text.p: A top lawyer for Brooke Group Ltd wrote a memo 34 years ago expressing concern that labeling the company's Lark cigarettes as "safer" could be interpreted as "less cancer-producing," NBC reported Sunday.

The network said it obtained secret documents in which the lawyer said marketing some of Liggett Group's cigarettes as safer could raise problems for the company's other cigarette brands and other tobacco companies.

Other documents obtained by the network included a 1988 draft report in which company lawyers expressed keen interest in chemical residues left on tobacco leaves from pesticides used in growing tobacco in the 1950s and 1960s, including several which have since been banned as unsafe.

Liggett, the maker of Chesterfield, L&M and Lark cigarettes, rocked the tobacco market last month when it announced that it was settling claims in 22 states, agreeing to turn over a portion of its profits to the states and curb advertising practices in exchange for immunity.

As part of the agreement, Liggett turned over internal company documents that Florida and other states hope to use to prove that cigarette makers knew of the addictive quality of cigarettes and hid that fact from consumers.
On Monday a judge in West Palm Beach is expected to rule on whether the documents fall under the attorney-client privilege as cigarette makers claim.
NBC said the documents it obtained were not part of those turned over by the company under its agreement.
